title: Terminal-site evaluation identifies ordinary modules and derived scalar extension
statement: Let $\mathcal T$ be the category with one object $*$ and only its identity arrow, equipped with the topology whose sole covering sieve is the maximal sieve. For a commutative ring $A$, let $\underline A$ be the ring sheaf on $\mathcal T$ with value $A$. Evaluation $E_A:\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A)\to A\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is an exact equivalence, with inverse assigning a module its one-object sheaf. It identifies sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] with ordinary module tensor [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], including its action on morphisms, and identifies direct-sum total tensors, cohomology, quasi-isomorphisms and K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Termwise evaluation therefore induces equivalences $K(\underline A)\simeq K(A)$ and $D(\underline A)\simeq D(A)$, compatible with the localization functors [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For any homomorphism $f:A\to A'$, these equivalences identify termwise sheaf change of rings along $\underline f$ with ordinary extension of scalars $-\otimes_A A'$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. They transport the universal total left derived pair (functor and its natural counit) [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] of the former to a universal total left derived pair of the latter. In particular the derived change of rings of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] becomes ordinary derived scalar extension, with the same resolution computation isomorphisms and derived-to-ordinary counit. No flatness of $f$ or boundedness of complexes is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03CW (definition-sheaf-modules), specialized to the category with one object, one arrow, and only the maximal covering sieve; the exact tensor equivalence and the transport of localization and universal derived pairs are the explicit terminal-site specialization of these definitions.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison] for the exact evaluation $E_A$ and inverse $I_A$, tensor and scalar-extension comparisons. On this site every matching family has one entry and its unique amalgamation is that entry. Thus sheafification changes no values; kernels, cokernels and direct sums are ordinary module constructions at $*$. The tensor comparison is $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes y$; tensor maps send it to $u(x)\otimes v(y)$. Iterated comparisons agree on pure tensors. For $f:A\to A'$, the same formula identifies the target scalar action and maps $u\otimes1$, hence $e_{A'}T_s\cong T_me_A$.

source.place: Tag 03CW (definition-sheaf-modules), explicit matching-family computation for the maximal sieve on the singleton identity category

proof.text: Evaluation and its inverse preserve coproducts. Tensor in either variable preserves small colimits by the module tensor universal property; their tensorators respect units and associativity on pure tensors. Apply [lem-sfb-termwise-strong-monoidal] to both $E_A$ and $I_A$ to obtain the natural direct-sum total-tensor chain isomorphisms, including both signed differential terms. Then [lem-trf-exact-tensor-equivalence-kflat-homotopy] gives the complex and homotopy equivalences, cohomology comparisons, quasi-isomorphism and K-flat equivalences, and the shift and cone compatibilities.

source.place: Tag 06YN (definition-K-flat), together with more-algebra.tex Tag 06XZ (definition-K-flat); derived.tex section-homotopy: the exact tensor-equivalence invariance argument for the acyclic total-tensor test, cohomology and homotopies, not a theorem asserted by these definitions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-ringed-scalar-universal-resolution-comparison] to the small site $\mathcal T$ and $\underline f$. It supplies the universal pair $(L_s,\varepsilon_s)$ for $F_s=Q'_sT_s$, identifies $L_s$ with derived change of rings and makes $\varepsilon_{s,P}$ invertible on every K-flat $P$, with its augmentation and resolution formulas. No flatness of $f$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes), dual assertion and equation-everywhere; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), proof in the fixed-site change-of-rings case. Explicit counit normalization for the ring-sheaf theorem lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-localized-universal-derived-pair-transport] with $e=e_A$, inverse $i_A$, quasi-isomorphisms as $W,W'$, and the derived localizations. Step 2 verifies $e_A(W)\subset W\prime$ and $i_A(W\prime)\subset W$. This constructs $d_A,j_A$ and their localization comparisons; likewise for $A'$. With $t=d_{A'}$, $F=F_s$, $G=F_m=Q'_mT_m$, step 1 supplies $tF_s\cong F_me_A$. The lemma gives $L_m=d_{A'}L_sj_A$ and its conjugated counit $\gamma:L_mQ_m\to F_m$, with the required universal natural-transformation bijection and counit-compatible derived comparison.

source.place: Tags 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization) and 04VK (lemma-properties-right-localization), combined with derived.tex Tag 05S9 (definition-right-derived-functor-defined) and equation-everywhere. Agent formulation of simultaneous localization and universal-pair transport, not a verbatim theorem of these tags.

proof.text: For any ordinary K-flat resolution $q:P\to M$, step 2 makes $i_Aq$ a sheaf K-flat resolution. The preceding two lemmas identify its computation with $\gamma_P\circ L_m(Q_mq)^{-1}$ and give $\gamma_M=F_m(q)\circ\gamma_P\circ L_m(Q_mq)^{-1}$. Their naturality and cocycle formulas identify all resolution comparisons and the derived-to-ordinary counit, including $M[0]$. This proves the asserted identification in the full unbounded categories.
